key_insight: A large pretrained video generation model (Cosmos‑Predict2) can be fine‑tuned with minimal changes to serve as an effective visuomotor policy and planner—removing the need for multi‑stage post‑training or new action‑generation architectures.
problem_solved: Prior attempts to adapt video models for robotics required complex multi‑stage pipelines and added modules to generate actions, making integration brittle and sample‑inefficient; this work simplifies the adaptation so spatiotemporal priors from video models can be directly leveraged for control and planning.
method: Start from a pretrained Cosmos‑Predict2 video model and fine‑tune it end‑to‑end on visuomotor datasets with simple action conditioning (minimal architectural changes).
Train the model to predict future observations conditioned on candidate action sequences and use its predicted futures to select or refine actions (planning / MPC style inference).

Keep training objectives and pipeline lightweight (behavior‑cloning / likelihood‑based fine‑tuning and optional online adaptation) to preserve pretrained spatiotemporal priors and improve sample efficiency.
impact: Provides a low‑complexity, high‑reuse path for turning large video models into practical visuomotor controllers and planners, lowering engineering overhead and improving long‑horizon reasoning for robotics and embodied AI.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video model → simple action conditioning/fine‑tuning → prediction → planning/MPC loop
Side‑by‑side rollouts: predicted future frames with overlaid action sequences vs actual robot execution
Performance chart: task success / sample efficiency comparing Cosmos Policy to prior multi‑stage baselines
Schematic illustrating planning over predicted futures (search/display of candidate action sequences and selected trajectory)
paper_title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
paper_authors: Moo Jin Kim, Yihuai Gao, Tsung-Yi Lin, Yen-Chen Lin, Yunhao Ge
